title: General Chemistry I
note: New course, built from the UNIBEN compendium (3 sittings, verified answer key). Organized into 10 topics covering the standard CHM101 syllabus.

questions.prompt: A gas has a density of 3.38 g/L at 40°C and 1.97 atm. What is its molar mass? (R = 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K)
questions.explanation: Using PV=nRT with n=mass/M and density=mass/V: M = ρRT/P = (3.38×0.0821×313.15)/1.97 ≈ 44.11 g/mol.

questions.prompt: A compound is found to contain 69.94% iron and 30.06% oxygen by mass. What is its empirical formula? (Fe = 55.85, O = 16.00)
questions.explanation: Moles Fe = 69.94/55.85 ≈ 1.252. Moles O = 30.06/16 ≈ 1.879. Ratio O:Fe ≈ 1.5:1, or 3:2 when scaled to whole numbers — giving Fe₂O₃.

questions.prompt: How many moles are present in 41.6g of ammonium carbonate, (NH₄)₂CO₃? (N=14, H=1, C=12, O=16)
Calculate the percentage of zinc by mass in ZnSO₄·7H₂O. (Zn=65, S=32, O=16, H=1)
The empirical formula of a compound is CH₂O and its molecular weight is 120. What is its molecular formula?
questions.explanation: Empirical formula mass = 12+2(1)+16 = 30. Multiplier = 120/30 = 4. Molecular formula = (CH₂O)₄ = C₄H₈O₄.

questions.prompt: An atmosphere consists of 79 mole% N₂, 17 mole% O₂ and 4 mole% O₃. The total pressure of the mixture is 0.75 atm. Calculate the partial pressure of O₃.
questions.explanation: By Dalton's Law, partial pressure = mole fraction × total pressure = 0.04 × 0.75 = 0.03 atm.

questions.prompt: A 1.00-litre sample of gas at 1.10 atm is compressed to 0.80L at constant temperature. What is the final pressure?
questions.explanation: By Boyle's Law, P₁V₁=P₂V₂: P₂ = (1.10×1.00)/0.80 ≈ 1.38 atm.

questions.prompt: Calculate the density of carbon dioxide (CO₂) in g/L at 760mmHg and 55°C. (C=12.01, O=16.00)
3g of CH₄ and 2g of H₂ are mixed and kept at 760mmHg and 273K. What total volume will the mixture occupy?
questions.explanation: Moles CH₄ = 3/16 ≈ 0.1875 mol. Moles H₂ = 2/2 = 1 mol. Total moles ≈ 1.1875 mol. At STP, V = n×22.4 ≈ 26.6L.

questions.prompt: 25.8L of a gas has a pressure of 690 torr and a temperature of 17°C. What will be the volume if the pressure is changed to 1.85 atm and the temperature to 345K?
questions.explanation: Using the combined gas law P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂, with P₁=690/760≈0.908atm, T₁=290.15K: V₂ = (0.908×25.8×345)/(290.15×1.85) ≈ 15.1L.
